messages:
zara: Quick follow-up to the rate/lease RFC. We observed a revoke -> immediate cross-shard re-admit loop causing eviction spikes.
ryan: Is the root cause stale revoke visibility across schedulers?
zara: Yep. Revokes write a KV tombstone but other schedulers only learn lazily. Clients keep asking other shards and get new leases.
meera: A pragmatic pattern: short-lived tombstone + edge LRU cache + async tombstone fetch. Admission flow:
1) fast local token check
2) consult local revocation cache
3) on cache miss, put client into probation path and async read KV to populate cache
This avoids blocking the normal happy path.
ryan: Fanout ping on revoke could prime caches but must be best-effort. Also add per-tenant revoke_seq so cache can detect newer revokes.
zara: TTL discussion: 15s/30s/60s candidates. Shorter TTL reduces collateral but widens window for thrash. For canary use 30s default and probation-only behavior (no hard-deny).
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary scheduled for revocation-cache + probation on 10% edge at 03:00 UTC for 2h.
meera: Ops playbook: manual retract steps, appeals for verified tenants (automated appeals go to probation), dashboards for new-lease-after-revoke metric.
ryan: Action items: meera -> draft ops playbook and appeal flow; zara -> micro-RFC with TTL presets and probation rates; meera/ryan -> prototype cache shim + histograms for tombstone read latency.
zara: Keep rollout conservative. First canary should only enable probation path so we gather signals before any hard-blocking. Thanks everyone.
